notes: (NW-6008): Out of scope: scalar core (with its L1 I-cache / D-cache, branch predictor and TLBs) is excluded from the energy model; gem5 stats are read only for numCycles and the instruction counts matching CustomMatMul(wVpush|iVpush|vpop)? and CustomV(exp|exp2|erf|tanh|sin|cos)
(NW-6008): Out of scope: CustomVlaneIdx instruction counts are deliberately not collected: it is lane-index generation, not an SFU op, and its energy is negligible

(NW-6008): Out of scope: BAR / MEMORY_BAR (barrier) instruction counters are not collected: synchronization is control-side work (scalar-core scope) and the stall time it causes is already inside total_exec_cycles, so it is charged as leakage over the window

(NW-6008): Out of scope: VCIX serializer/deserializer (the vector <-> systolic-array interface) is not modeled as a separate component: its push/pop events are already charged at both endpoints (w_reg writes, vpu_spad reads/writes), and PyTorchSim exposes no serdes size parameters — the remaining mux/wire datapath is second-order

(NW-6008): Out of scope: DRAM background/standby power and the NPU-side memory controller / HBM PHY are not charged: vendor IDD/standby currents for HBM are not public (no open HBM power tool exists), so the dram compound charges command energies only (activate / read / write / refresh, constants cited from O'Connor & Chatterjee et al., MICRO 2017); the on-chip consequences of DRAM traffic (VMEM fills/drains, DMA engine, NoC flits) are charged by their own compounds
(NW-6001): 6 non-MAC kernel(s) use the f32 datapath of MAC kernel mouppepddmz.

(NW-2209): Activity stat 'CustomMatMul' (total 5280 in 11 window(s)) is not charged, because projection 'pytorchsim' waives it: compute is charged as useful MACs (useful_macs action) plus idle PE cycles (array_idle_slots action); this instruction count is a redundant counter of the same work

(NW-2209): Activity stat 'comp_gemm_ops' (total 10560 in 11 window(s)) is not charged, because projection 'pytorchsim' waives it: COMP GEMM op counter: the same GEMM work is charged per systolic active cycle (CustomMatMul action); charging both would double-count

(NW-2209): Activity stat 'comp_vector_ops' (total 66 in 17 window(s)) is not charged, because projection 'pytorchsim' waives it: COMP vector op counter: the same vector work is charged per vector-unit active cycle (vpu compound actions); charging both would double-count

(NW-2209): Activity stat 'systolic_active_cycles' (total 6510 in 11 window(s)) is not charged, because projection 'pytorchsim' waives it: the active cycles of the arrays are split into useful_macs and array_idle_slots, which the systolic_mac actions charge; the raw cycle count also gives the share of each array
(NW-6014): The window names come from kernels.yaml.
(NW-2116): User component 'example_68000_cpu_core' (user_components.yaml) is in the library, but the run does not use it.

warnings.message: mouppepddmz: the gem5 counts are scaled by the tile graph (3 compute nodes, 769 executions).
warnings.explain: gem5 simulates the sample program of the kernel: each compute node of the tile graph one time. NPUWattch multiplies the counts of each node by its executions in the kernel. The tile graph file (*_tog.py in the kernel directory) gives the executions. The totals agree with the COMP counts of the TOGSim log. No action is necessary.

warnings.message: mouppepddmz: 6291456 useful MACs of 6291456 active PE cycles (100.0%), the other PE cycles are charged as idle.
warnings.explain: TOGSim reports the active cycles of the systolic array, not how many PEs hold a real weight. NPUWattch computes the useful MAC count from the operator and the tensor shapes. It charges this count in the compute mode of the PE. It charges the other active PE cycles in the idle mode, in which the PE is clocked and holds its data. No action is necessary.
